subject: Request: carveout for customer-controlled network in Private deployment
messages:
From: Daniel Cole <ops+contracts@cascadebio.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: legal@cascadebio.com
Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Request: carveout for customer-controlled network in Private deployment

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We are moving to a Private deployment in our AWS account (us-west-2) and have a couple of procurement items to close out before we sign the order form. One open ask from our legal/infra teams: because the VPC, BGP peerings, and most of the network path are managed by Cascade, we need an explicit carveout in the SLA for customer-controlled network events (e.g., transit provider outages, on-prem VPN flaps, misconfigured route tables, and MTU/DF issues) that impact connectivity to Redwood-managed inference nodes.

Specifically, we propose the following:
- Redwood commits to 99.90% service availability for the inference service when network to the customer RDS/peers is healthy.
- Incidents attributable to customer-managed network or third-party transit (including BGP propagation, peering misconfiguration, or external maintenance windows we do not control) are excluded from uptime calculations.
- Redwood will provide a post-incident report for network-bound incidents with diagnostic logs (time-series latency, TCP/RST counts, and connection failure traces) within 72 hours.

I attached a simple network diagram to show the points of control. Our procurement asked if you can confirm that this carveout won't materially affect your support/response commitments and whether Redwood can offer a recommended handshake (health-check endpoints, BGP health probes, or a small monitoring agent we can run in our VPC) to make incident classification deterministic.

Are you able to share proposed contract language and any operational recommendations? We need to close this week to meet our internal go-live date.

Thanks,
Daniel
Director, Infrastructure
Cascade Bio
Attachments: cascade-network-diagram.pdf (PDF)
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Daniel Cole <ops+contracts@cascadebio.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: carveout for customer-controlled network in Private deployment

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear write-up and the diagram. Appreciate the tight timeline; we can move fast on this.

Quick answers up front:
- High-level: yes, Redwood is open to a narrowly scoped carveout for customer-managed network incidents, with mutual rules for evidence and classification.
- We can provide a proposed SLA addendum and a draft incident playbook showing what telemetry we need to classify "network-owned" vs "service-owned" incidents.

Two quick clarifying questions for your infra team before we draft language:
1) Do you have an existing (and shared) maintenance calendar for your transit providers / VPN windows?
2) Can you run a lightweight connectivity endpoint (HTTP ping + TLS handshake) from an instance in your VPC to a Redwood health URL? If so, we can add health-check criteria to the addendum which will make exclusions faster to validate.

I'll loop in Neha from Product Security and Marcus from Contracts for the exact carveout wording. We'll aim to get a draft back in 24 hours.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Manager
Redwood Inference
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: carveout for customer-controlled network in Private deployment

Folks — forwarding Cascade's ask. Key points: customer-managed VPC + transit; wants carveout language and deterministic classification (health checks, telemetry). They want draft this week.

My suggested stance:
- Product: ok to exclude incidents that are clearly outside our control given mutually agreed evidence (customer reachability checks, cloud flow logs, and our agent-side metrics). We should require joint incident reviews and a standard evidence checklist.
- Contracts: propose a limited exclusion clause listing specific failure modes (BGP/peering/transit outages, customer router misconfig, on-prem VPN flaps), plus SLA credits are only payable for incidents classified as Redwood-owned after review.
- Security: require that the customer allow collection of the following artifacts for excluded incidents: IP-level connection diagnostics, TLS handshake traces, and timestamped health check results. No packet capture.

Questions for you both: what language would you prefer ("network-owned incidents excluded from uptime calculations" vs "network incidents will be subject to joint classification and excluded when agreed"), and do we want to require a minimal health-check (HTTP/TLS) as a gating criterion?

-- Soojin

On Tue, May 9, 2028 at 09:12 Daniel Cole <ops+contracts@cascadebio.com> wrote:
> Hi Soojin,
> 
> Thanks again for the walkthrough... (see original)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 May 2028 10:23:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Request: carveout for customer-controlled network in Private deployment

Suggested contract language (first pass):

"Network Responsibility Carveout. For Customer Private Deployments where the customer controls the network infrastructure (including but not limited to VPC routing, VPN/Direct Connect, transit providers, and peering arrangements), outages or degradations attributable to Customer-controlled network components or third-party transit providers shall be excluded from Redwood's availability calculations, provided that: (a) Customer promptly provides evidence requested by Redwood for incident classification (e.g., cloud flow logs, timestamped client health checks, and the results of Redwood's connectivity probes); (b) both parties perform a joint classification within five (5) business days following remediation; and (c) exclusion is applied only to incidents for which Redwood's diagnostic data demonstrates no service-level fault within the Redwood-managed runtime (e.g., no process crashes, successful KV cache reconciliation, and expected responses from the local inference endpoint)."

Operational addendum (bullet summary):
- Required telemetry: customer-side HTTP/TLS health-check (endpoint: https://health.redwood-inference.com/ping/<customer-id>), cloud VPC flow logs for incident window, and Redwood runtime logs for the same interval.
- Classification workflow: joint triage call within 24 hours, draft post-incident report within 72 hours, final classification + credit decision within 5 business days.
- Support SLA impact: Redwood support commitment remains unchanged for any incident where Redwood diagnostics show service misbehavior. For excluded incidents, Redwood will provide diagnostic assistance and remediation guidance but will not be responsible for credits.

I recommend we send this as a short addendum PDF, include a proposed timeline for the joint triage, and offer a lightweight health-check script they can run in their VPC (we can provide a CloudWatch-friendly script).

I'll attach a draft addendum and a one-page checklist for their infra team. If you want, I can take the lead on the DocuSign flow once they sign off.

- Marcus

Attachments: proposed-sla-addendum-20280509.pdf (PDF)
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Daniel Cole <ops+contracts@cascadebio.com>, legal@cascadebio.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 10 May 2028 14:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: carveout for customer-controlled network in Private deployment

Hi Daniel —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached is a short SLA addendum and an operational checklist that matches our suggested classification workflow. Key bullets:
- Explicitly excludes customer-network and third-party transit failures from uptime calculations when the evidence checklist is satisfied.
- Requires a lightweight customer-run health-check (we've included a one-line curl + TLS check you can run from an EC2 instance) and shared VPC flow logs for the incident window.
- Joint classification timeline (triage within 24 hours, draft report in 72 hours, final decision within five business days).

If that looks good, we can route the addendum through DocuSign this afternoon: https://docusign.net/ABC-123. Marcus will own the contract signature path; Neha will own the operational checklist items.

Next steps: can you confirm you can run the health-check by EOD today and share an upcoming maintenance calendar for your transit providers? Once we have that, Marcus will send the DocuSign packet.

Appreciate the quick coordination.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Manager
Redwood Inference
